A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ThinkingViT and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained experiments can be matched across substantial reformatting, renumbering, and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet classification, throughput, robustness, routing, and ablation results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original classification experiments and reports additional segmentation, Swin, early-exit comparison, and token-reuse/pruning results.

M1.justification: The core nested subnetworks, Token Recycling, joint losses, and entropy-based stopping remain unchanged. v2 adds a Swin-S adaptation that keeps the first architectural stage intact while initially halving the other stages, and an optional DynamicViT pruning component in the second inference round. The batching pseudocode documents inference rather than establishing a changed core algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds semantic segmentation on ADE20K and Cityscapes, extending evaluation beyond ImageNet-family classification to dense prediction and urban scenes. The existing ImageNet variants remain covered. Swin is an architectural extension, while DETR remains future work rather than evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Figure 8 adds Swin-T/S/B comparisons and six early-exit comparators: SDN, PABEE, BERxiT, ViT-EE, PCEE, and LGViT. Figure 14 adds A-ViT and AdaViT; Figure 9 compares Segmenter backbones. The depth-expanded controls in v1 Table 1 disappear. The earlier appendix Early Exit baseline is retained under the name BranchyNet, with unchanged results.

E3.justification: New segmentation evaluations introduce mIoU under single-scale and multi-scale inference with a linear Segmenter decoder, while the new early-exit comparison uses Swin backbones. The DynamicViT combination specifies a 0.8 pruning ratio. v2 also exempts the new KV-cache experiment from the retained ablations' stochastic-training setup. These are added experimental settings, not evidence that retained ImageNet experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds targeted tests of KV-cache reuse and compatibility with DynamicViT, plus qualitative segmentation examples comparing inference rounds. It removes the depth-expansion control in Table 1. Existing head-expansion, loss-weighting, fusion, entropy, and prediction-dynamics analyses largely remain; moving the head-expansion analyses to Appendix K does not make them new.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the results. The statement about roughly 100 prototyping runs remains unchanged. Prediction entropy is a routing signal, not newly added statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds segmentation, Swin, early-exit, and pruning-combination results. Section 4.6 reports 83.5% accuracy at 9.5 GMACs for the Swin adaptation, and Table 4 adds KV-cache accuracies of 73.872% and 75.674% across rounds. Table 1 changes the one-extra-iteration cost from 3.45 to 2.5 GMACs and removes depth-expanded results. Most retained ImageNet results, including the entropy-threshold table, are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation of nesting, token fusion, joint training, and entropy stopping is retained, with equation splitting and renumbering. v2's weighted-average GMACs formula explains the existing compute metric; it does not introduce a new theoretical result. Neither version supplies substantive theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central adaptive-width and Token Recycling contributions, including the headline 2.0/2.9 percentage-point ImageNet claims, remain unchanged. v2 adds explicit main-text claims of demonstrated segmentation and Swin transfer and superiority to depth-adaptive methods. These refine and extend applicability claims whose broader architectural motivation already appeared in v1.

C2.justification: v1 Section 4.5 presents uniformly hard inputs as an efficiency limitation; v2 Section 4.8 recasts the retained evidence as successful routing and continued superiority, dropping the explicit efficiency warning. The discussion of hierarchical token-alignment difficulties is also removed. v2 adds interpretations of segmentation refinement and demonstrated pruning complementarity, while retaining training-overhead and excessive-expansion limitations in Appendix I.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies inference batch size 512, validation-set throughput aggregation, GMAC accounting, and filtering/rebatching pseudocode in Appendix J. It also documents Swin stage allocation and the pruning ratio. Reported training hardware changes from A100 to H100, without establishing reruns of retained results. Code access is unchanged, and detailed training settings for the new applications remain sparse.

R1.justification: v2 adds a substantial early-exit discussion distinguishing adaptive depth from ThinkingViT's progressive width, covering methods such as MSDNet, SDN, PABEE, BERxiT, LGViT, and JEI-DNN. It adds references supporting segmentation, Swin, A-ViT, and AdaViT, while removing works including Once-for-All, LLaMaFlex, MatMamba, and Sliced Recursive Transformer. This expands research positioning beyond bibliographic reformatting.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the abstract, method overview, hard-input discussion, and conclusion around a broader application narrative. It removes the isomorphic-architecture subsection, reorganizes evaluation and appendices, and moves head-expansion/loss-weighting explanations into Appendix K. These are substantial structural and narrative revisions alongside the added scientific content.

P2.justification: The paper changes from a predominantly single-column layout to two columns, swaps the opening performance and architecture figures, merges ImageNet comparison panels, and splits other appendix panels. Ablation tables move into the supplement. New Swin, segmentation, and qualitative figures, expanded pruning plots, and batching pseudocode substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The segmentation and Swin experiments provide substantial empirical support for portability claims that v1 largely left untested. Broader early-exit comparisons address an important alternative to progressive width, while pruning integration and inference-measurement details strengthen practical validation. These gains outweigh sparse settings for the new experiments and the less explicit treatment of the hard-input efficiency limitation; the improvement comes from stronger validation, not higher retained ImageNet scores.
